Area Forecast Discussion...UPDATED
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
323 AM PST Mon Nov 23 2026

UPDATED AVIATION SECTION 

.SYNOPSIS...23/202 AM.

A few showers will linger off the Los Angeles county coast
this morning. Otherwise, mild and dry conditions are expected
into Tuesday. Light rain is possible again Tuesday night into
Wednesday along the Central coast. Thanksgiving will be dry and 
warmer.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-WED)...23/202 AM.

Frost advisories are currently in effect through this morning for
the Antelope valley and eastern adjacent foothills. The expected 
minimum temperatures are 33-35 and locally down to 32 degrees. 
Other interior areas will approach advisory thresholds but will 
likely fall short due to clouds inhibiting the nighttime 
raditional cooling process. Low clouds and fog is expected to 
develop overnight across interior areas of SLO county including 
the Salinas Valley. These clouds should burn off by late morning. 
In addition, a few showers may linger near Catalina island. 

Weak ridging and offshore pressure gradients are expected to 
develop over the region on Tuesday. LAX-DAG falls to -2 mb
with minimal upper-level support - thus expecting light offshore
winds with warm and dry conditions. High temperatures in the
60s-70s will be common across the coastal and coastal valleys. 

A decaying cold front will approach the central coast Tuesday
night into Wednesday morning. Current trends in guidance has 
decreased precipitation - with amounts generally 0.10" or less.
For Ventura and Los angeles counties, the chances for measurable
rain are less than 10%. As for temperatures, there will actually 
be a bit of warming for most areas on Wednesday as an upper level 
ridges noses in behind the weak front.

.LONG TERM (THU-SUN)...23/202 AM.

For Thanksgiving Day and Black Friday, the combination of 
a strong upper level ridge (588-590 DM) and weak to moderate
offshore pressure gradients will bring warm and dry conditions
to the region. High temperatures will peak on Friday with
coast/coastal valleys reaching mid 70s to lower 80s and about
10 degrees cooler across interior sections. Most locations
will average 8-12 degrees above seasonal norms. Northeasterly
winds are expected to remain below advisory levels due to
limited upper level support. However, there could be some local
gusts in the 40-45 mph range Thursday morning across the 
western San Gabriels and Santa Susanna mtns. A very low chance
that a wind advisory will be needed. 

There is a strong signal that troughing will return to the area
at the end of the month heading into December. We will have to
keep an eye on the potential for a series of systems but details
are blurry this far out. Stay tuned for updates.

&&

.AVIATION...23/1123Z.

At 1009Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer nor an inversion.

Overall, moderate confidence in 12Z TAF Package. LIFR FG at
KPRB thru 23/17Z (+/- 2 hrs). LIFR FG likely to return near
24/10Z. 30% chance of periodic LIFR conds at KSBP thru 23/15Z. 
Otherwise, VFR conditions are expected thru forecast period.

KLAX...Good confidence in VFR TAF. Any east wind component is 
expected to remain below 7 kts thru the forecast period.

KBUR...Good confidence in VFR TAF. No wind issues expected.

&&

.MARINE...22/724 PM.

High confidence that winds and seas will remain below small craft
advisory (SCA) levels through Tuesday night.

Two storms are expected to affect the area. The first is crossing
the waters this evening and will move clear of the area later
tonight. Another storm will move over the area Tuesday night
through Wednesday. The second systems will bring the best chance 
of rain to the seas north of Pt Conception. Post- frontal low-end 
SCA level NW-W winds will be possible Wednesday/night south of 
Point Conception. A significant westerly swell (around 14-16 feet)
is expected mid- week, with large, SCA level seas for the outer 
waters.

&&

.BEACHES...22/746 PM.

There is significant concern for moderate to major coastal 
flooding Thanksgiving week. This is due to the combination of 
kelvin wave/thermal expansion, Perigean spring tides, and a large
long-period westerly swell (260-280 degrees).

===============================================================

[For Central Coast, Ventura, and Los Angeles counties]:

A COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY is in effect for Monday- Tuesday.

Potential impacts: shallow flooding of beach parking lots and 
unprotected roads, moderate beach erosion likely, isolated damage 
to structures/building/roadways but could occur but is unlikely. 

A COASTAL FLOOD WATCH is in effect for WEDNESDAY- THURSDAY.

The swell will arrive during this period which will combine with 
the aforementioned factors. Still some uncertainty in regards to 
how timely these will combine, but regardless significant impacts 
seem probable. Timing of peak high tides are expected between 845 
AM-1000 AM and predicted values are: roughly 8.2-8.4 ft for 
LA/VTA and 7.9-8.2 ft for Central Coast. The reasonable worst case
scenario is 0.3-0.5 ft above these values. A slight limiting 
factor that may prevent the worst case scenario from materializes 
would be higher mean sea level pressure.

Potential impacts if upgraded to COASTAL FLOOD WARNING:

More extensive moderate coastal flooding reaching further inland,
moderate to high risk of damaging flooding of coastal roads and 
structures, and significant beach erosion is likely.

Areas of greatest concern: Morro Bay, Pismo Beach, Oceano Dunes, 
& Cayucos/Avila/Pismo Piers. For LA: Santa Monica to Palo Verdes 
and Long Beach/Naples. For VTA, Faria to Silver Strand Beach 
including inside of harbors and Ventura Harbor.

A HIGH SURF ADVISORY has been issued for the Central Coast from 
Sunday morning through Thursday afternoon.

Surf of up to 11 feet expected Monday morning with a lull in high
surf Monday night into Tuesday followed by rapid building to 
10-15 feet Wednesday morning and to 15 to 22 feet Wednesday 
afternoon and evening. There is an increasing likelihood the High
Surf Advisory will need to eventually be upgraded to a High Surf 
Warning probably by Tuesday. There is also a risk of breaking
waves in the Morro Bay Entrance early Wednesday through Wednesday
night and possibly into Thursday. 

For the Ventura and Los Angeles County beaches, elevated to high 
surf is expected for much of the upcoming week, peaking Wednesday 
and Thursday with likely High Surf Advisories. There is even the 
small chance of Warning-level surf up to 15 feet for the Ventura 
County coast during this period and a risk of breaking waves in
the Ventura Harbor Entrance early Wednesday through Wednesday
night. 

==================================================================

[For Santa Barbara South Coast & Catalina/Santa Barbara islands]:

A COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY has been issued for Monday-Thursday.

Potential impacts: shallow flooding of beach parking lots and 
unprotected roads, moderate beach erosion likely, isolated
damage to structures/building/roadways but could occur but is
unlikely. 

Areas of greatest concern: Santa Barbara to Rincon and Jalama
Beach. 

Additional Information: Elevated to high surf is likely through
Thanksgiving week. Additional coastal hazards will likely be
needed for Friday.

==================================================================

In conclusion, this is a particularly concerning period for 
coastal flooding risks and high surf - Please read the "actions" 
section below. 

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS:

(1)Heed advice from local officials - Rely on their expertise
regarding preparedness, closures, and warnings. 

(2)Protect property - Take necessary actions such as setting up
sandbags or barriers in flood-prone areas.

(3)Avoid flood areas - Stay clear of rock jetties, and flooded
roads, walkways, and other normally dry places.

(4)Stay off the beach - large breaking waves can cause injury, 
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near 
shore.

(4)Monitor the forecast for latest information: weather.gov/LOX
and @nwslosangeles on social media. Be aware of when high tide
peaks in your area: tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov. Refer to LAXCFWLOX.
